answer: Prism-Ripple Lock Each agent must anchor their identity to a unique, verifiable ripple in a decentralized ledger—specifically, a cryptographic hash derived from a public transaction timestamped within a shared crystal lattice. To register, an agent submits a valid ripple; duplicates are rejected by consensus. The enforcement rule checks that no two identities share the same ripple origin or timing window. An attacker attempting to clone must generate new ripples through computationally expensive mining-like work, paying full network fee rates per attempt.
